tools.name: as_of
tools.description: The state of one document as it stood on one date. Pure lookup, no ranking. mode=outline lists provisions without text and may be narrowed with anchors; mode=select returns only the named anchors' text; mode=full (default) returns the whole text. Every provision carries its own permalink and hash.

tools.name: timeline
tools.description: Every publisher state a document has been in: timeline intervals, version keys, and explicit timeline_semantics. Legilux intervals describe applicability; EUR-Lex intervals describe official consolidated wording states, not entry into force.

tools.name: in_force_on
tools.description: Compatibility name for publisher states covering a date, computed from timeline intervals and deduplicated by work. Legilux states describe applicability; EUR-Lex states are official consolidated wording states and must not be called entry into force. Every envelope carries timeline_semantics and th

tools.name: diff
tools.description: What changed between two dates for one work: which publisher versions cover the selected dates and, where both texts are held, retrieve them via as_of to compare. An optional held article anchor scopes the typed comparison workspace. Read timeline_semantics before describing legal applicability.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Filtered legal search. keyword is deterministic FTS5/BM25; hybrid adds the pinned local encoder and fixed RRF when verified vectors are mounted. No generative model participates. The response query_plan separates resolved work constraints, article and role intent, and residual provision terms. Retur

tools.name: article_history
tools.description: Every distinct text ONE provision (article/annex) has had on its publisher timeline, plus lifecycle events (inserted/removed/renumbered, renumbering detected mechanically by identical text hash). Read timeline_semantics before calling an interval legal applicability. Answers "what did Article X say

tools.name: provenance
tools.description: Proof chain for one lex_id: source URI, retrieval time, record/body hashes, event chain, corpus commit, index build, stamp signature.

tools.name: coverage
tools.description: What we hold and what we lack, tier by tier: counts, date ranges, history_begins, known gaps. This tool exists to say what we do NOT have.

tools.name: cited_by
tools.description: Which held provision versions contain captured publisher cross-references to this work. This reverse lookup reports the publisher references Lex captured; it does not classify their relationship type or assess current legal effect.

tools.name: changes_in_period
tools.description: ACROSS the corpus: which works gained new versions between two dates, how many each, and when — the aggregate counterpart of diff/timeline (which cover ONE work). Use for "what changed between 2025 and 2026", "which laws changed most during the pandemic", "what moved last month". order=by_churn rank

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "article_history" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "cited_by" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
